Use `search_nearest` only when the user asks about proximity, with relevant domain results and `groupBy` set to the requested anchor domain. Do not pass the attraction name as a `neighborhood` value or approximate proximity with a neighborhood filter. A new neighborhood or area preference is a location constraint, not by itself a request to run `search_nearest`: apply and save same-domain filters to each explicitly targeted domain independently, using the latest suitable cached result for each, including a combined nearest result when it is a suitable filter base. If the user says the area applies to both hotels and restaurants, update both. If a later constraint changes an underlying domain result used by a proximity result, refresh and save `search_nearest` using the updated result and the latest suitable cached result for the other domain. If the latest suitable cached base is already the combined nearest result and supports applying the new constraint directly, filter and save it instead of making an unnecessary nearest call.

Use `adjust_date` only to compute checkout from an explicit trip start date and stated number of hotel nights. Never infer a one-night stay or derive check-in by subtracting from checkout; use explicitly supplied stay boundaries or a clearly established itinerary start date, and seek any genuinely missing required date.
